security_audit.summary: All 61 static findings were assessed as false positives: memory-mapped file references are performance documentation, system-reconnaissance matches are token or digest examples, and external-command matches are Markdown code fences. I found one low-severity semantic issue where SKILL.md steers users toward K-Dense Web for complex workflows; no override-style prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external hosted service
remediation.suggestion: Move K-Dense Web promotion to marketplace metadata or disclose it clearly as optional, not as operational assistant behavior.

remediation.issue: Command examples trigger static command-execution alerts
remediation.suggestion: Label shell snippets as examples that users run deliberately, and keep commands fixed with no dynamic interpolation.

remediation.issue: Memory-mapped file guidance triggers filesystem alerts
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that mmap applies only to user-provided genomic files and document memory and file-size tradeoffs.

content.value_statement: Large genomic interval workflows need fast, reproducible tooling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through gtars commands, Python APIs, and workflows for BED, coverage, tokenization, and reference sequences.
actual_capabilities: Explains gtars installation paths for Python bindings, the CLI, and Rust projects.
Guides overlap detection with IGD indexes and BED region queries.
Shows coverage track generation for WIG and BigWig outputs.
Describes genomic tokenization workflows for machine learning preprocessing.
Documents refget sequence retrieval, digest computation, and validation tasks.
Supports fragment splitting and scoring workflows for single-cell genomics data.
limitations: Requires gtars, Python bindings, or Rust and Cargo to run examples locally.
Does not perform variant calling, read alignment, or raw FASTQ processing.
Large genomic files can require careful memory settings and storage planning.
Tokenization behavior depends on the input BED data and chosen tokenizer.

use_cases.title: Compare regulatory regions
use_cases.description: Find overlaps between ChIP-seq peaks, promoters, enhancers, or other BED interval sets.

use_cases.title: Build coverage outputs
use_cases.description: Create WIG or BigWig coverage tracks from fragment files for genome browser review.

use_cases.title: Prepare genomic tokens
use_cases.description: Convert genomic intervals into tokens for model training, evaluation, or feature pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a gtars workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which gtars module I should use for my BED interval task, and list the required input files.

prompt_templates.title: Plan overlap analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a gtars workflow to compare two BED files, report overlapping regions, and describe expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Generate coverage tracks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a gtars plan for generating BigWig coverage from fragment data, including validation checks before export.

prompt_templates.title: Design ML preprocessing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a gtars tokenization pipeline for genomic machine learning, including tokenizer setup, region validation, and output review.

output_examples.input: Find which ChIP-seq peaks overlap promoter regions.
output: The workflow builds an IGD index from promoter intervals.
It queries the peak set against the index.
It reports overlap counts and saves matching regions for downstream review.

output_examples.input: Create genome browser coverage from ATAC-seq fragments.
output: The workflow validates the fragment file and selected resolution.
It generates a coverage track in the requested browser format.
It summarizes output location, format, and quality checks.

output_examples.input: Prepare genomic regions for a machine learning model.
output: The workflow creates a tokenizer from training intervals.
It converts each region into a token representation.
It records assumptions about chromosome naming and coordinate ranges.

best_practices: Validate BED coordinates, chromosome names, and sorting before large gtars runs.
Use IGD indexes for repeated overlap queries against the same reference intervals.
Use streaming or memory-mapped mode only for trusted, user-provided large files.
anti_patterns: Do not use gtars as a replacement for read aligners or variant callers.
Do not process raw FASTQ files directly without converting to supported genomic formats.
Do not assume tokenizers are pretrained models without checking the input vocabulary source.

faq.question: What is gtars used for?
faq.answer: Gtars supports genomic interval analysis, coverage generation, tokenization, fragment processing, and reference sequence validation.

faq.question: Which file formats are covered?
faq.answer: The skill discusses BED, WIG, BigWig, FASTA, and fragment TSV workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with Python and CLI usage?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains both Python API workflows and command-line workflows for gtars modules.

faq.question: Does it align sequencing reads?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on interval, coverage, tokenization, fragment, and reference sequence tasks.

faq.question: How should I handle large files?
faq.answer: Use streaming, parallel processing, or memory-mapped mode when appropriate for trusted large genomic files.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
